skill.description: Structured code review skill for changed files, with checks for OWASP Top 10 risks, ORM performance issues, logic bugs, and project coding standards.

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown reference examples that document unsafe and safe code patterns for reviewers. The executable helper script only lists git changes and does not show command injection, network use, or secret access. Two semantic issues remain: hardcoded absolute local file reads and review guidance that may modify code without explicit approval.

remediation.suggestion: Replace author-specific absolute paths with repository-relative paths and ask before reading files outside the active project.

remediation.issue: Immediate edits during a review workflow
remediation.suggestion: Change the action step to report findings first and request confirmation before applying fixes, unless the user explicitly asked for edits.

remediation.issue: Scanner noise from vulnerable reference examples
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly labeled as non-executable documentation and avoid presenting them as implementation snippets.

semantic_findings.title: Hardcoded Absolute Local File Reads
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read author-specific absolute home-directory paths. A marketplace skill should not direct agents to read local files outside the active project without explicit user confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 48 and 49 explicitly name absolute local paths to read. The intent is project standards lookup, but the behavior can cause unintended local file access.

semantic_findings.title: Unapproved Code Modification During Review
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md tells the agent to fix critical and important issues immediately during a review. This can change user code when the user requested review-only feedback.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The action section directly instructs immediate fixes for serious findings and only asks approval for recommended issues. This is a clear integrity risk in review workflows.

content.user_title: Review Code Changes for Security and Performance
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss security flaws, performance regressions, and project standards. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a structured review of changed files.
actual_capabilities: Identifies changed files with git diff commands.
Reviews code against OWASP Top 10 vulnerability patterns.
Checks SQLAlchemy usage for N+1 queries and missing indexes.
Looks for logic bugs, edge cases, and error handling gaps.
Compares Python and backend changes against documented project standards.
Formats review findings by severity with explanations and suggested fixes.
limitations: Works best inside a git repository with committed or uncommitted changes.
Project standards references are specific to the original Geist repository.
It is guidance for AI review, not a replacement for tests or security scanners.
Some reference files include vulnerable examples for education only.

use_cases.title: Review Backend Changes
use_cases.description: Check modified Python files for security issues, ORM problems, and logic defects before merge.

use_cases.title: Screen Security Risk
use_cases.description: Use OWASP-focused prompts to find injection, access control, XSS, and unsafe deserialization patterns.

use_cases.title: Enforce Project Standards
use_cases.description: Compare changed files with team conventions for models, agents, imports, and dependency choices.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Change Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you want a quick review of current changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current git changes. List security, bug, and performance findings first, with file and line references.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before merging code that handles user input or sensitive data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changed files for OWASP Top 10 issues. Focus on injection, access control, secrets, XSS, and unsafe deserialization.

prompt_templates.title: Performance and ORM Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for backend or database changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changed backend files for performance risks. Check SQLAlchemy queries, eager loading, indexes, loops, and large result handling.

prompt_templates.title: Full Standards Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a final review before a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full review of changed files. Apply project standards when available, prioritize critical issues, and separate required fixes from optional improvements.

output_examples.input: Review changed backend files before a pull request.
output_examples.output: Findings grouped by severity, including a SQL injection risk, an N+1 query warning, and recommended fixes.

output_examples.input: Check this diff for OWASP Top 10 issues.
output_examples.output: A security review that calls out vulnerable input handling, missing authorization checks, and safer implementation guidance.

output_examples.input: Review these SQLAlchemy model changes for performance.
output_examples.output: A performance report with notes on missing indexes, eager loading needs, and unnecessary full-object loading.

best_practices: Ask for review after changes are small enough to inspect carefully.
Run tests and linters after applying any suggested fix.
Confirm repository-specific standards before treating style feedback as required.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill as the only security gate for production code.
Do not apply broad refactors during a focused review without user approval.
Do not trust vulnerable examples in reference files as production-ready code.

faq.question: Does this skill edit code automatically?
faq.answer: The skill contains guidance about fixing serious issues, but users should request or approve edits before changes are applied.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run security scanners?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and references. Separate scanners and tests should still be used.

faq.question: Can it review frontend code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes checks for XSS, dangerous HTML rendering, and general logic issues.

faq.question: Why are there vulnerable code examples?
faq.answer: They are reference examples that show what reviewers should identify and avoid.

faq.question: Is it tied to one repository?
faq.answer: Some standards mention the Geist repository. Adapt those references for other projects.
